findings.finding: Young children find it harder to remember complete routines, so primary dance education emphasizes listening to beats and practicing beginner steps to rhythm.
findings.quote: Younger children have a harder time remembering full dance routines, so it is important that they focus more on listening to the beats of the music and practicing beginner moves to the rhythm.

findings.finding: Self-kindness serves as a strong positive predictor of life satisfaction in recreational dance settings.
findings.quote: Self-kindness emerged as a strong positive predictor (β = 0.258, p p p = 0.029) negatively predicted life satisfaction.

findings.finding: Learner-centered strategies like reflection, dialogue, and choice often correlate with positive cognitive, self-related, and psychosocial outcomes.
findings.quote: results revealed that learner-centered features (reflection, dialog, collaboration, observation, and choice) were more often associated with more favorable cognitive, self-related, psychosocial, and implementation outcomes.

findings.finding: Synchronized movement, collaborative choreography, and shared rhythm help foster prosocial behaviors such as peer connection, cooperation, and empathy in adolescents.
findings.quote: Mechanisms such as synchronized movement, shared rhythm, and collaborative choreography facilitated these effects.

findings.finding: Self-taught learners can analyze their movement quality by video recording themselves while dancing.
findings.quote: One can also film oneself dancing to better understand how different moves look, or solicit feedback from others.

principle: Dance education relies on varied pedagogical approaches—from structured guidance to learner-centered reflection, self-compassion, and collaborative movement—to foster technical skill, self-expression, and well-being.
for_the_teacher: Focus younger learners on listening to the musical beat and practicing basic moves to the rhythm rather than memorizing long routines.
Integrate self-kindness training into lessons to cultivate emotional resilience and protect against self-judgment.
Provide options for reflection, learner choice, and dialogue during class to support self-related and cognitive development.
Encourage learners to record video of their own practice to evaluate their execution and track progress.
when_it_does_not_apply: Conclusions regarding learner-centered pedagogy remain tentative due to heterogeneity in study designs, outcomes, and risk of bias across reviewed studies.
